LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers were defeated by the Detroit Lions by the score of 20-17 on Sunday afternoon. Despite two missed field goals by rookie Trey Smack and numerous highly questionable penalties called on the defense, the Packers had every opportunity to win the game. As it stands, though, they fell to 4-3 with the loss. Early in the game against Detroit, the Packers lost starting center Sean Rhyan to an ankle injury, and his backup, Jacob Monk, to a quad injury. Earlier today, Monk was placed on injured reserve, and the fear is that Rhyan suffered a high ankle sprain that could keep him out for several weeks. As Green Bay hurries to field a full active roster for Thursday night, they released their initial injury report despite the fact that the team did not practice today. All participation statuses are estimations: As can be seen from the post above, cornerback Benjamin St. Juste was listed as a full participant. This is good news for the Packers secondary, who have been without him for the past several weeks. Aaron Banks, who was active on Sunday, was a limited particpant. Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 8: DL Anthony Campbell (ankle): He played 28 snaps in Detroit, so expect him to play Thursday night unless there was some setback. LB Zaire Franklin (shin): The defense's captain will miss his second consecutive game after injuring his leg in practice last Thursday. It's possible he could be back after the mini-bye in Week 9. Expect Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper to play all the snaps at inside linebacker. C Sean Rhyan (ankle): He is expected to miss up to a month after suffering a high ankle sprain on Sunday in Detroit. John Williams is the assumed starter at center for Thursday night, but the Packers weren't willing to confirm starters at center or right guard beforehand. Guard Aaron Banks and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste do not have a status designation on the final injury report and are good to go for Thursday night. Banks was active last week but did not play. away.headline: Bucs-Panthers Inactives | Baker Mayfield Returns to Action
away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. The Buccaneers and Panthers submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Seven meeting at Bank of America Stadium. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. home.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET. home.headline: NFL rumors: Packers star Micah Parsons gets potential return date
home.blurb: “Packers star Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week and make his 2026 debut in November, with the most likely return date coming Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams,” NFL insider Tom Pelissero posted on X, formerly Twitter. The Green Bay Packers ’ wait to have Micah Parsons back on the field is almost over. The star pass rusher, who has been rehabbing his injured knee, is nearing his much-awaited season debut, with one game in particular looking likely . Parsons was traded in August 2025 to the Packers by the Dallas Cowboys, then agreed to a record four-year, $188 million contract. He was having a fantastic debut season for Green Bay, recording 12.5 sacks in 14 games. However, he suffered a torn ACL against the Denver Broncos in December and missed their playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite missing Parsons, the Packers have had no problems getting to the opposing quarterback this season. They currently lead the league with 22 sacks , including six on Bryce Young in their 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night. But of course, it will still be a huge boost for the Packers to add one of the most dangerous pass rushers in the entire league in Parsons to a defense that has already been making a ton of plays under new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. Aside from leading the league in sacks, they also have a league-leading 10 interceptions. But before potentially getting Parsons back in Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams, the 5-3 Packers have two more tough games to go. They will go to Foxboro to take on the New England Patriots. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. Lamar Jackson (ankle) has not played since the first half of Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, but he is expected to return on Sunday in what has suddenly become a huge game for the Ravens. Baltimore is 4-3 this season after going 1-2 in the games Jackson missed, and it’s in last place in the AFC North with every team in the division over .500. The Ravens dropped back-to-back key division games against Cleveland and Cincinnati without the two-time league MVP. Josh Allen – the MVP favorite this season – and the Bills are coming out of their bye week to play in this game, and they’re favored at home after a 5-1 start. Buffalo is looking to get the top spot in the AFC, and it benefitted from a Kansas City Chiefs loss (now 5-1 as well) during Week 7. Sunday’s game is the eighth meeting between Jackson and Allen all-time, with the Ravens holding a 3-2 edge in the regular season while Allen has won both of his playoff matchups against Jackson. Who has the edge in this regular-season clash? All season long, the SI Betting team has been predicting the final score of NFL games, and this one is no different. Oddsmakers are expecting this to be a high-scoring game, even though it's Lamar Jackson's first game back after a three-game absence due to an ankle injury. The total in this matchup is all the way up at 54.5, and it's worth noting that the last time these teams met in the regular season, they combined for 81 points. There are a ton of awesome playmakers in this game, including Derrick Henry, James Cook, Zay Flowers, Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore and others that could make an impact by scoring a touchdown. So, why don't we bet on a few players to do exactly that? The anytime touchdown scorer market is one of the most exciting ways to bet on the NFL, especially when two of the league's top quarterbacks – Jackson and Josh Allen – are facing off. While Henry, Cook, and Allen are all set at minus odds to find the end zone, I've decided to look at three players at plus money that could score in Week 8. Here's a breakdown of the odds for these picks and my analysis ahead of Sunday’s Raves vs/ Bills clash. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Ravens vs. Bills Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Zay Flowers Anytime TD (+165) Ravens star Zay Flowers has been one of the best receivers in the NFL this season, catching 40 of his 53 targets (in six games) for 608 yards and three scores. Flowers has three games with double-digit targets, and he’s by far the No. 1 option in this passing game. Now, with Jackson expected to return, Flowers should get a major boost against a defense that has not been able to guard anyone in the passing game. After all, the Bills are dead last in the league in EPA/Play on defense. Buffalo’s pass defense is one of the worst in the league, ranking 29th in EPA/Pass while allowing 15 passing scores. Opposing wide receivers have torched the Bills, scoring 11 touchdowns across six games – the most allowed to the position in the NFL. It doesn’t get much better for Flowers, who is averaging over 100 yards per game and has caught at least five passes in every matchup. Since these teams combined for 81 points the last time they played, I’d expect another up-and-down matchup with a ton of offensive possessions for both sides. Flowers has simply been too effective in space, and he has the fourth-highest target share in the NFL this season. That puts him in a great spot to find the end zone for the second week in a row on Sunday. Dalton Kincaid Anytime TD (+210) Dalton Kincaid has just one touchdown for the Bills this season (in Week 2), but the Ravens have struggled to defend the opposition, allowing five tight end touchdown receptions in seven games. Kincaid was an afterthought in the Bills’ offense in Weeks 3, 4 and 5, receiving just seven total targets, but Joe Brady made a point of getting him involved in Week 6. The former first-round pick had eight targets, reeling in seven passes for 38 yards. While it wasn’t a huge day for Kincaid, he had a touchdown negated because of a penalty. I’m buying the Bills star in this matchup, especially since the passing offense has run a lot smoother for Buffalo when he’s one of the top options. Ja’Kobi Lane Anytime TD (+320) Third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane has appeared in just three games for the Ravens this season due to a wrist injury, catching eight of his 13 targets for 76 yards. He’s yet to find the end zone in the NFL, but with Jackson returning, I’m buying the rookie at this price in Week 7. I’ve already mentioned how awful this Buffalo pass defense is, and if the Bills end up selling out to slow down Flowers, Lane is the next-best option. Lane has seen his snap share rise in back-to-back weeks, playing nearly 70 percent of the offensive plays in Week 6. If every game on the NFL Week 8 board was a house decorated for Halloween, Sunday's battle between the Baltimore Ravens and Buffalo Bills would be the place handing out full-size candy bars. Lamar Jackson is back for Baltimore, giving football fans just the treat we wanted: a showdown with Buffalo QB Josh Allen. My Ravens vs. Bills predictions lean into that QB competition and what could be the most fun game on Sunday's slate. Here are my best NFL picks for this AFC heavyweight bout on Nov. 1. TOP Pick Ravens vs Bills prediction: Bills moneyline The return of Lamar Jackson has understandably dragged down the market on the Buffalo Bills . That offers a better ask on the home team's moneyline. The former MVP comes back from an ankle injury just in time, as this offense was getting stale under backup QB Tyler Huntley . But Jackson isn't 100% and his mobility will be tested early by the Bills defense, with the 11th-highest pressure rate per dropback. Baltimore's offensive line might not be up to the challenge, with injuries stacking up. Making plays with his legs has been a huge part of Lamar's success in recent meetings with Buffalo, rushing for 54, 70, and 73 yards in their three most recent matchups. Buffalo has had two weeks to rest and prep for Jackson and the Ravens , coming off a Week 7 bye. That also allows the Bills to get difference makers back on both sides of the ball, including WR1 D.J. Moore and DE Ed Oliver . Not only is Buffalo holding the rest edge, but this is its first home game in new Highmark Stadium in nearly a month. The last time the Bills were in front of the Mafia faithful, they were upset by the rival Patriots in Week 4. A win over Baltimore puts Buffalo back in the driver's seat of the AFC. Ravens vs Bills combo I'm siding with the Bills to pick up the win at home, leaning on Josh Allen to come through like he always does and for this Buffalo pass rush to make Jackson feel uncomfortable under center. Allen's nose for the end zone is incredible, and he's scored four total touchdowns in his last two meetings with the Ravens. Allen already has eight rushing touchdowns in six games this year and rumbled for 14 last year, including two touchdowns against the Ravens in their Week 1 shootout. away.headline: Ravens announce 3 roster moves before Week 8 showdown with Bills
away.blurb: Baltimore announced the transactions one day after releasing its final injury report, which listed Tampa as questionable with a knee injury. His activation makes him eligible to play against Buffalo and adds depth to a secondary preparing to face Josh Allen and the NFL's highest-scoring offense. His return is particularly important because safety Jaylinn Hawkins is ruled out with a knee injury. Although Tampa plays cornerback rather than safety, his availability gives defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver another option in the defensive backfield and on special teams. The Ravens also elevated Edoga to provide offensive line depth after starting right guard Vega Ioane was ruled out with a knee injury. Ioane suffered an MCL sprain during Baltimore's 35-13 loss to Cincinnati and returned to practice Thursday and Friday, but the rookie will miss Sunday's contest. Edoga has previously been elevated for Baltimore's games against Atlanta and Cleveland. His availability gives the Ravens additional flexibility along an offensive line that must protect Lamar Jackson and improve its rushing production. Baltimore Ravens – baltimoreravens.com Isaac, meanwhile, provides depth at outside linebacker as Baltimore continues adjusting to the loss of Tavius Robinson, who was placed on injured reserve after the Cleveland game. Isaac was elevated for last week's matchup against Cincinnati and will again be available to contribute on defense and special teams. Baltimore enters Sunday's contest at 4-3 after consecutive losses, while Buffalo is 5-1. Jackson is expected to return after missing three games with a high ankle sprain, giving the Ravens an opportunity to regain offensive momentum. The Baltimore Ravens made three roster moves Saturday ahead of Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills , activating cornerback T.J. Tampa Jr. from injured reserve while elevating offensive tackle Chuma Edoga and outside linebacker Adisa Isaac from the practice squad. Tampa was placed on injured reserve Sept. 19 and returned to practice earlier this month. The cornerback participated fully Thursday and Friday, allowing Baltimore to evaluate his progress before making Saturday's roster decision. home.blurb: Baltimore announced the transactions one day after releasing its final injury report, which listed Tampa as questionable with a knee injury. His activation makes him eligible to play against Buffalo and adds depth to a secondary preparing to face Josh Allen and the NFL's highest-scoring offense. His return is particularly important because safety Jaylinn Hawkins is ruled out with a knee injury. Although Tampa plays cornerback rather than safety, his availability gives defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver another option in the defensive backfield and on special teams. The Ravens also elevated Edoga to provide offensive line depth after starting right guard Vega Ioane was ruled out with a knee injury. Ioane suffered an MCL sprain during Baltimore's 35-13 loss to Cincinnati and returned to practice Thursday and Friday, but the rookie will miss Sunday's contest. Edoga has previously been elevated for Baltimore's games against Atlanta and Cleveland. His availability gives the Ravens additional flexibility along an offensive line that must protect Lamar Jackson and improve its rushing production. Baltimore Ravens – baltimoreravens.com Isaac, meanwhile, provides depth at outside linebacker as Baltimore continues adjusting to the loss of Tavius Robinson, who was placed on injured reserve after the Cleveland game. Isaac was elevated for last week's matchup against Cincinnati and will again be available to contribute on defense and special teams. Baltimore enters Sunday's contest at 4-3 after consecutive losses, while Buffalo is 5-1. Jackson is expected to return after missing three games with a high ankle sprain, giving the Ravens an opportunity to regain offensive momentum. The Baltimore Ravens made three roster moves Saturday ahead of Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills , activating cornerback T.J. Tampa Jr. from injured reserve while elevating offensive tackle Chuma Edoga and outside linebacker Adisa Isaac from the practice squad. Tampa was placed on injured reserve Sept. 19 and returned to practice earlier this month. The cornerback participated fully Thursday and Friday, allowing Baltimore to evaluate his progress before making Saturday's roster decision. With Tampa activated and two additional players elevated, Baltimore has addressed several roster needs before facing one of the AFC's strongest teams. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Heading into Week, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans have everything to prove, but also nothing at all. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions for Titans vs. Bengals: Faith in a Tennessee Win is Lost After Simmons Trade Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI It's a dour week of staff predictions here at Titans On SI, as we all collectively mourn the team's loss of DT Jeffery Simmons. The Titans are bound to take a hit due to trading away their best player, and that hit comes to a head against the Cincinnati Bengals tomorrow. Last week, the staff went 1/4 due to Tennessee losing to the Browns. Isaiah was the only one to forecast a Titans loss. This week, the rest of us are following his lead. With multiple key players confirmed to sit for the Titans and big roster questions still looming, here's our slate of predictions for Tennessee vs. Cincinnati in Week 8. Lane: Bengals 30, Titans 17 I'm both highly optimistic about the future of this Titans team and terribly pessimistic about their current state. You don't trade Jeffery Simmons and get away with it now and later. I think Tennessee pays for his loss in Week 8. The Cincinnati Bengals have scored 30+ points in two straight weeks, and against a freshly weakened Tennessee defense, I expect that trend to continue. Cam Ward is likely to struggle without Carnell Tate, but the Titans' offense should be able to find relative momentum between the red-hot Tony Pollard and reliable second-year WR Elic Ayomanor I just can't imagine this one going the Titans' way, even then. Isaiah: Bengals 30, Titans 17 Fresh off a competitive loss to the Browns, where the offense scored a season-high 24 points, it's hard not to feel optimistic heading into Cincinnati. However, I believe the Titans are already punting on the season, especially after dealing their best player, DT Jeffery Simmons, to Chicago this week. The Bengals are top-10 in points scored and fewest points allowed, which is not an ideal matchup for Tennessee. I can't trust QB Cam Ward to keep the Titans in the game. The Bengals are a high-powered offense led by QB Joe Burrow, who boasts a 4-1 record all time against Tennessee. Shaun: Bengals 36, Titans 16 Following the franchise-altering trade of DT Jeffery Simmons, the Titans have the chance to prove a lot of doubters wrong on Sunday. Unfortunately, this game is a complete mismatch on paper, especially now that Simmons is gone and WR Carnell Tate being ruled out with a shoulder injury. It’s the type of game that can get out of hand relatively quickly if Tennessee doesn’t come out firing. QB Cam Ward will likely need to match the Bengals’ offensive firepower, and without Tate, an already tall task ultimately becomes too much to overcome. In the end, I think a strong performance by QB Joe Burrow and company results in a hardly competitive 20-point win at home. Dharya: Bengals 31, Titans 20 After trading Jeffery Simmons, I expect Tennessee to come out with extra motivation for this game. The Titans should be able to this contest close, but at the end of the day, Cincinnati possesses too much talent and explosiveness on offense. With how Brian Daboll's offense has played this season, a shoutout with the Bengals isn't winnable for Tennessee. I was already wary of the Tennessee Titans' motivations heading into their Week 8 road date with the Cincinnati Bengals. Then Tennessee traded All-Pro DT Jeffery Simmons to Chicago Thursday afternoon. That move tacked on an extra point to this surging spread, with Cincinnati now laying -11.5 on Sunday afternoon. My Titans vs. Bengals predictions size up that mountain of chalk as well as the crater Simmons leaves in this Tennessee stop unit. Here are my best NFL picks for Nov. 1. TOP Pick Titans vs Bengals prediction: Over 46.5 One of my first plays of Week 8 was taking the Over in this game. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping out his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange, I like the Over even more considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Baltimore stop unit in the second half of Sunday's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. Tennessee's secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While the Titans haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't played many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring but don't discount the Titans. Tennessee is playing with pace and faces a Cincy defense that still has work to do. Chase Brown finds the end zone to the cheers of fantasy owners everywhere. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Tennessee secondary giving up explosive plays. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Titans vs Bengals touchdown scorer: Chase Brown If anyone was happy to see Simmons traded before Week 8, it was Bengals running back Chase Brown. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Tennessee red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, Tennessee had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. Due to that drought, we're getting a discount on his ATTD market in Week 8 considering this prop was trading around 60% two games ago. Given the massive spread, Cincinnati will be in a run-positive game script in the second half of Sunday, helping boost Brown's TD probabilities. His TD forecasts range between 60% and 78%, given he's a threat to run one in or catch a touchdown pass. Titans vs Bengals player prop: Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Cincinnati has arguably the best one-two punch at receiver in the NFL, with Tee Higgins serving as "Robin" to Ja'Marr Chase's "Batman". But don't tell Higgins that. He looked more like Superman in Week 7, putting in a monster effort in the win over the rival Ravens. He caught six of seven balls his way for 148 yards and a touchdown. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. We mentioned the Titans' problems giving up home runs over the top, and Higgins is one of the best deep threats in the land, averaging 21.6 air yards per reception and amassing eight catches for 20+ yards. Tennessee has also been burned by WR2s to start the season, rating 24th in DVOA vs. WR2s at FTN while giving up almost 56 yards per game to those second options. Higgins' Week 8 models are very bullish on his receiving yards, ranging from 65 to a high of 91. Most forecasts come in above 80 yards, and my projection sits just shy of 81 yards receiving. Much of the NFL is still grading the trade, but the Cincinnati Bengals are likely relieved by the timing, as they host the Titans this week. This matchup pits two teams that seem to be going in opposite directions. Tennessee is 1-6, and their offense is struggling to gel together around quarterback Cam Ward. Meanwhile, Cincinnati just took off like a jet last week, scoring 35 unanswered against the Baltimore Ravens. It seems pretty clear-cut how this game is expected to play out, but how do oddsmakers and experts feel about it? The Bengals are currently 11.5-point favorites against the Titans, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the biggest spread Cincinnati has had this season. They were only 6.5-point favorites against the Miami Dolphins coming off two straight losses. Safe to say the number got a little bigger after Tennessee traded Simmons this week. The point total is set at 46.5 points combined. The real wild card for these bets is which Bengals' defense is going to show up. Are they going to give up 200 rushing yards, or will they be able to shut it down like last week against Derrick Henry? All of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has a consensus of Cincinnati winning from their six experts None of NFL.com's five experts are taking the Titans NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick Initially, I was worried this may be a trap game at home for the Bengals. Sometimes this team will just drop a terrible game after a huge win. That happens especially when they are playing down to a bad team's level. I'm not sure how the Simmons trade might impact that, but I am hopeful the Titans are a bit more deflated coming out than fighting even harder. Either way, Burrow and this offense shouldn't have any trouble scoring and moving the ball. Their job got a lot easier without Simmons in the middle of that defense. They just don't have the offense to keep up in a shootout. We all long for the day when the Titans aren't a double-digit underdog in any game they play. That will take them getting really good on at least one side of the ball. That shouldn't be that hard with the way the NFL is set up. home.headline: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans
home.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. home.headline: Ja'Marr Chase's absence from Bengals practice gets an explanation in latest injury report
home.blurb: Chase (ankle) officially had a rest day, but is also listed with an ankle injury. He was seen in the locker room after practice. The "rest" being listed as the primary reason for his DNP insinuates it is not a serious injury, but seeing what the rest of his week looks like will be key before Sunday's game. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during last Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens and is back to being "week-to-week." Coach Zac Taylor has already declared Dugger out for this week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen got his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle was limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) was also limited. Four Titans did not practice due to injuries including their first-round pick, WR Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate has played in all seven games for Tennessee this season, catching 34 passes for 413 yards and a touchdown. Fellow receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) went limited. He's been dealing with his hip injury for the last week and missed last Sunday's game because of it. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) was also a DNP. He's been playing next to All-Pro Jeffery Simmons and has produced 13 pressures and 1.5 sacks in seven games. Backup running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) were also non-participants Wednesday in Nashville. Meanwhile, at least one person thinks the Dallas Cowboys don't need trade deadline help. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. The Cowboys are 3-4, but they play in a woefully weak NFC East. They're still favored to win the division. It's a far different world for the Cardinals, who stand at 2-5 and are buried in last place in one of the NFL's toughest divisions, the NFC West. Let's take a look at what to expect. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cowboys QB Dak Prescott will throw 3 TD passes again Prescott didn't have to do much against the Eagles as the Cowboys ran the ball at will. But he still had three touchdown throws. This will be more of the same, with a lot of runs and Prescott finishing off drives with TD passes. No matter what Stephen A. Smith says, Prescott is still that dude. Of course, it seems like Smith will say anything to keep his show in the spotlight. He questioned whether the Cowboys still have confidence in Prescott on First Take via Sports Illustrated. "This is my interpretation," Smith said. "I believe there's a lack of confidence, supreme confidence in Dak Prescott. You believe in him, you're paying him, but in the same breath, you're understanding the importance of having that balanced running attack. Because when you just have him dropping back the pass that football, you're not satisfied with the level of production that you're getting." Whatever. The only way Prescott might not have a big game is if the Cardinals' defense gets gashed for 5-, 10-, and 20-yard TD runs. Oh, well, that is possible. The Cardinals have a rotten defense. Cowboys WR George Pickens will catch multiple TD passes Here's the trick: Prescott will be able to pick and choose who he wants to get the TD catches. And since Lamb has already been well established with six TD receptions in 2026, look for Prescott to make sure Pickens, who has two, closes the gap. With 16 fewer catches than Lamb on the season, it's not a stretch to see Pickens get double-digit grabs in this contest. Now, Pickens is banged up, but it's probably one of those mid-week no-biggies. The injuries are to his shoulder and hamstring, according to NBC Sports. "Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new," Aditya Fuldeore wrote. "He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status." Both receivers are supremely confident , as Lamb expressed, according to dallasnews.com. "I think that's pretty self-explanatory, to be honest," Lamb said. "Once we get going, I don't think there's … nah, I know for a fact, there's not a person in this league that can stop us." And Pickens said he's learning patience. "It's just super important just because that can boost the morale of the team when you just wait your turn," Pickens said. "Whether you're a running back, tight end, you make your play that boosts the offense." Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will throw for 280-plus yards It has been an up-and-down season for the veteran quarterback. But this is a game where volume will lead to yardage, even if it is in a game that winds up with a no-so-close loss. Brissett seems to be on the verge of losing his starting job. So look for him to be focused and effective at times. Head coach Mike LaFleur said the offensive issues aren't all on Brissett, according to NBC Sports. "Like I told you guys, he's still the starter," LaFleur said, via transcript from the team. "It's collective. Again, if the ball was just stagnant for 60 minutes and you couldn't even cross the 50-yard line, it'd be one thing. We've been down inside the 10-yard line 10 times over the last two games, so the ball is moving, but we have to finish jobs. Again, that starts with me, but that's a collective effort. "The players have to go execute. And I have to put them in better positions and give them the clarity to go do so. When they do have that clarity, they have to make the plays. We know that. We're not going to shy away from that. We know we have to finish the job when we're down there, and I don't even think we're having these conversations right now [if we had]." Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 8 Status Revealed
away.blurb: Jeremiyah Love has battled an ankle injury throughout the season, but he could make his long-awaited return to the field in Week 8. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, he did not play in Week 7. While nobody knows for sure if he will play in Week 8, the team's official practice report notes the running back returned to the field in a limited capacity, which bodes well for this week. home.blurb: Locke is one of two Cowboys safeties to land on injured reserve this season, along with Jalen Thompson, who has yet to be designated to return as he deals with a hamstring issue. Schoonmaker was added on Thursday and did not practice over the last two days of the week before drawing a questionable tag. Based on the elevation of Mitchell, it's a good bet that Schoonmaker won't suit up on Sunday. The Dallas Cowboys have made a few roster moves ahead of their Week 8 game against the Arizona Cardinals. The team announced it has activated safety P.J. Locke off injured reserve, which gives Dallas' struggling defense a much-needed reinforcement for Sunday afternoon. In addition to that move, the Cowboys have elevated tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad. One of the team's offseason free-agent signings , Locke has not appeared in a game since Week 2 after suffering a foot injury in that contest that forced his placement on injured reserve. Thompson was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 and was initially expected to miss four to six weeks. He is now four weeks into that timeline, so he could be back in the next few. With Locke back, he should slot into a starting role next to Malik Hooker, which will push Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell down on the depth chart. However, don't be surprised if Clark still sees a good amount of playing time, as he has shined for Dallas in the absences of Locke and Thompson. Th elevation of Mitchell comes amid uncertainty surrounding tight end Luke Schoonmaker, who popped up on the injury report this week with a groin issue. A former fifth-round pick of the Detroit Lions, Mitchell was signed to the Cowboys' practice squad in early September after cutdown day. Assuming he plays on Sunday, this will be his first game action of 2026. Mitchell has appeared in 35 games (one start) over four seasons in the NFL and has recorded 16 catches for 169 yards. His best year was his rookie season in 2022, when Mitchell reeled in 11 receptions for 113 yards. Mitchell hasn't proven to be a reliable blocker during his four-year career, but he does have the ability to make a dent in the passing game if called upon. We'll know for sure if Schoonmaker or Mitchell will be active when the Cowboys drop their inactives at around 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday morning. home.headline: Eagles Week 7 injury report vs. Cowboys: Are Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith playing?
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles have different answers on two offensive stars entering Week 7 against the Dallas Cowboys . DeVonta Smith is out with a hamstring injury, while Saquon Barkley remains questionable despite finishing the practice week as a full participant. Barkley’s Saturday upgrade is encouraging, but it does not confirm he will play. Philadelphia must still prepare for the possibility of being without its featured running back alongside an already unavailable receiving weapon. Barkley progressed from limited participation Thursday and Friday to full participation Saturday while managing his hamstring injury. That is a positive practice trajectory, particularly compared with remaining limited or missing the final session. However, the Eagles retained his questionable designation. The appropriate conclusion is that playing remains possible, not that he has been cleared for an unrestricted role. The loss is significant. Smith has 26 catches for 310 yards and two touchdowns in four appearances this season. He caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown against Carolina in Week 6, making his absence another interruption after a productive return. Philadelphia also ruled out Dontayvion Wicks , who missed all three practices with an ankle injury. Losing both receivers reduces the available options and complicates how the offense distributes opportunities. Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers are questionable despite three full practices, reinforcing why participation alone cannot settle availability. Landon Dickerson followed Barkley’s progression, moving from two limited practices to full participation Saturday. He remains questionable with knee and pectoral injuries, adding uncertainty to the blocking picture. Defensively, Michael Carter II and Nolan Smith are out after three missed practices, with abdomen and concussion injuries, respectively. Jonathan Greenard is questionable after missing Friday and Saturday with an ankle injury. Jalyx Hunt remained limited throughout the week and is questionable, as is Jakorian Bennett despite full participation. Smith’s situation is settled after three missed practices. Barkley’s is not, leaving the Eagles to balance optimism about his progress with uncertainty about his availability and potential workload. home.blurb: FRISCO, Texas (KMID/KPEJ) – The Dallas Cowboys are looking to build on their momentum after picking up a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. home.headline: Injury Report: Week 8 vs Cowboys
home.blurb: The Cardinals had been cautious with the rookie running back, but after three practices, the coaching staff felt Love was healthy enough to return. "Even though he's he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys by November 1st are truly at 100 (percent)," coach Mike LaFleur said. "But he's feeling as good as he can feel you know so yeah kind of go from there." Who will be blocking for him might be the bigger question. Center Hjalte Froholdt is questionable to play after being limited on Thursday with a knee injury. He did not practice on Friday. If unable to play, Hayden Conner could slide to center and the Cardinals would start a different player at right guard for the fourth time this season. Defensively, some reinforcements could be on the way. After missing the last three weeks, safety Dewey Wingard (knee) logged a full week of practice. He is questionable to play, as is cornerback Max Melton after he missed last weekend with a knee issue. Dallas ruled out wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf). Six players are questionable to play including defensive tackle Kenny Clark (back) and wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring). Wide receiver Michael Wilson (ribs) wore the yellow non-contact pinny for a second consecutive day. He told the media on Wednesday it is out of caution. Wilson was one of eight players limited for practice. Center Hjalte Froholdt appeared on the injury report and was limited with a knee injury. His status this weekend will be important to monitor since backup center Hayden Conner is currently playing right guard. The Cowboys were back at practice on Thursday. They opened up the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. Safety Caleb Downs (ankle), wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring), and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams (hamstring) were limited. Wide receiver Michael Wilson was wearing a yellow non-contact jersey. He appeared on the injury report with a ribs issue. He was limited. Multiple players returned to practice after being inactive on Sunday. Jeremiyah Love (ankle), safety Dewey Wingard (knee), cornerback Max Melton (knee), and quarterback Carson Beck (back) were limited. Cornerback Kei'Trel Clark was limited with an illness. Since the Cowboys did not practice on Wednesday, the designations were estimations. Wide receiver George Pickens was limited and listed with a shoulder and hamstring issue. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going.
