picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions will face a second straight NFC North divisional opponent when they take on the Minnesota Vikings Sunday afternoon. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North is officially the most explosive division in football, and Ford Field will serve as ground zero this Sunday. The 4-2 Detroit Lions are fresh off a thrilling, last-second 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. They are set to host the league's final remaining undefeated juggernaut: the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings. This Week eight clash is a textbook battle of strengths. Head coach Dan Campbell has Jared Goff playing at an early-season MVP level, engineering an electric offense. Meanwhile, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is piloting a historic, blitz-heavy defensive unit that is suffocating opposing quarterbacks. With massive divisional implications on the line, here are three bold predictions for this highly anticipated rivalry game. 1. Jared Goff Extends Interception-Free Streak to 7 Games Despite Massive Blitz Brian Flores' defense leads the NFL in blitz percentage (38%) and thrives on turning ordinary passing downs into an absolute nightmare. The Vikings' defense has already forced 11 takeaways and racked up 21 sacks. Statistically, Flores loves to force opposing quarterbacks into hurried mistakes. The first bold prediction is that Jared Goff will throw for over 275 yards, multiple touchdowns, and maintain a completely clean sheet with zero turnovers. Goff is currently on an unbelievable heater, throwing 14 touchdowns to zero interceptions through six games. While Flores will throw a kitchen sink of disguised coverages and loaded fronts at him, Goff boasts a stellar 127.1 passer rating against the blitz this season. Shielded by one of the best offensive lines in football, Goff will stay calm in the pocket, pick apart the blitz, and keep the football safe. 2. Jahmyr Gibbs Cracks 120+ Rushing Yards The Vikings have given up very little through the air, ranking near the top of the league in passing defense. However, if their elite unit has a minor vulnerability, it is on the ground. Last week, the Indianapolis Colts exposed some cracks by carving up Minnesota for 154 rushing yards. The second bold prediction is that Jahmyr Gibbs will erupt for over 120 rushing yards and a touchdown. Gibbs has been an absolute workhorse for Detroit, averaging an astounding 103.3 rushing yards per game. Though Flores historically found success neutralizing Gibbs last season, Drew Petzing's offensive scheme will counter Minnesota's aggressive defensive stunts by leaning heavily on the ground game. Gibbs will tire out the Vikings' pass-rushers, hit the secondary at full speed, and log his biggest performance of the year. 3. Lions Hand the Vikings Their First Loss of the Season Minnesota's 6-0 start has been heavily reliant on their elite defense. Kyler Murray and the Vikings' offense have regularly stalled, ranking 29th in total yards per game and managing just 20.7 points per game. To make matters more difficult, starting running back Aaron Jones Sr. is severely limited with a knee injury. The final bold prediction is that the Detroit Lions will win a high-scoring thriller, handing Minnesota its first loss of the 2026 season. The returning presence of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch gives Detroit's secondary the physical playmaking identity needed to keep Justin Jefferson under wraps. Ford Field will be deafening, and Detroit's offensive versatility will simply be too much to contain for all four quarters. Expect the Lions to walk away with a definitive statement win to tighten the race for the NFC North crown.

away.headline: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return)
away.blurb: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return) Skip to main content SI.COM Minnesota moved to 6-0 after getting past the listless Colts, and also came out of the game relatively healthy as an added bonus. A few Vikings did leave the game with injury, though, so there are a few names to watch this week ahead of a date with the Detroit Lions. Vikings who could return in Week 8 Price took a big hit on a punt return and was evaluated for a concussion. He was cleared to return to the game, but head coach Kevin O'Connell did say that Price was dealing with a stinger after the win. It didn't seem to affect the star returner, and there shouldn't be much concern heading into Week 8. Still, Price is one of those players that is darn-near irreplaceable for the Vikings if he did have to miss time. The Vikings' first-round pick exited the game with an apparent lower-body injury. And while his name didn't come up postgame as a possible serious injury, Banks' two previous foot injuries that forced him out of football for almost a year are certainly at the forefront of fans' minds. Banks didn't return after limping off the field , and his status will be something to monitor throughout the week. Luckily, the Vikings didn't appear to lose anyone to a long-term injury on Sunday. The key Vikings out for the season remained the same with Donovan Jackson, Josh Oliver, Jamal Adams and Tyler Batty all already lost for the year. With various injuries on offense, defense and even one on special teams, here's who should be fine, and who might miss some time for Minnesota. Like Price, Addison was evaluated for a concussion before being cleared to play shortly after. Still, he wasn't able to do much in the contest, notching just two catches for 20 yards. Addison had already missed the Week 5 contest with a hamstring issue, but it appears he should have a clean bill of health to try and right the ship heading into the Lions matchup. Jones has been battling a knee injury all season, and once again aggravated it late in the game against the Colts. O'Connell called the injury day-to-day after the game, but it wouldn't be too surprising if Jones needs a week off to let things heal. The Vikings have ridden Jones hard this season with Jordan Mason's own injury issues, and the toll on his body is adding up quickly. If Jones can't shake this nagging knee issue, the Vikings could look to make a move for another runner at the trade deadline . Still, Jones has given his all this season, and it's hard to see him voluntarily coming off the field. Obviously injury concerns have been a big talking point with Banks, and if he does have to miss time, fellow rookie Domonique Orange could get some more run . Last week the Jets lost a hard fought game to the defending AFC champions New England Patriots. That was understandable. Much less understandable was today's 28 – 25 loss at home to the previously winless Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins dominated the action for most of the game, building a two touchdown lead at halftime and maintaining an 11 point lead with less than five minutes remaining in the game before a late Jets touchdown made the score look closer than the game actually was. This loss came against a Dolphins team that had never held a lead at any point in the season prior to today. Today the Dolphins never trailed. It was a humiliating performance by the Jets. The horrendous Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-5 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Now the Jets look to get back on the winning track as they stay home to take on the 3-4 Las Vegas Raiders in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Raiders' defense has collapsed in their four game losing streak, surrendering 30+ points in each of the four games. With the trade deadline less than two weeks away, the sense of urgency for the Raiders in this game is high. Las Vegas enters this contest with injuries on both sides of the ball. away.headline: New York Jets Rule Out T'Vondre Sweat for Las Vegas Raiders Game, List David Bailey as Doubtful
away.blurb: Officially ruled out are massive defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat and edge Joseph Ossai. On the cusp of being officially declared out is edge David Bailey, who has missed all three practices this week with a groin injury. He is listed as doubtful on the injury report, and his absence would be a big blow to any Jets hopes of taking down the Raiders. Linemen Darrell Jackson Jr., Nate Lynn and Harrison Phillips will be asked to step into the breach on defense for the Jets. Lynn had a sack against Miami (his first, along with his first NFL tackle), while Jackson has done well in limited appearances. Phillips, who has played for the Vikings and the Bills, has been less successful. His PFF grade is an abysmal 49.2, ranking 102 out of 126 qualified linemen. But he is a big body and will have to step up in the absence of Sweat, who has been a rock in the middle for the Jets. Listed as questionable is running back Breece Hall, who has been out since Week 3 with a quad injury. He was limited during this week’s practices. “He’s a key cog of what we’re doing,” head coach Aaron Glenn said of Hall. “And each time he goes out [and practices], man, there are certain points that he has to hit to make sure that we’re all good and we want to make sure we hit those points.” If Hall plays – a game-time decision – he will likely see limited action and share the backfield with Allen, who has been the No. 2 rusher in the NFL for the time period he’s taken over from Hall as the lead back. Left guard Dylan Parham was given a surprisingly good injury update. He fully participated in practice on Friday and will likely see at least spot duty. He’s been out with a knee injury since Week 3 against Detroit, but was playing as well as any Jets lineman when he went down. The New York Jets will be severely depleted on the defensive line for their Sunday game against the Las Vegas Raiders. The injury news on the other side of the ball is a bit brighter for the Jets. Running back Braelon Allen has been cleared after fully practicing on Thursday and Friday. Allen had a minor ankle injury sustained in the Miami game. The Raiders have a much better health situation than the Jets. The only definite scratch was edge Patrick Johnson. Tight end Brock Bowers practiced fully this week, a big plus for the Raiders, who often use two tight ends.

away.headline: NFL Week 7 Injury Report: Raiders' Quay Walker and Rams' Puka Nacua Listed
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Quay Walker has been downgraded to questionable with a chest injury ahead of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. The change raises uncertainty about his availability for the Week 7 matchup at Allegiant Stadium. ESPN's Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden reported the downgrade on X on Saturday. Walker had been a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders' official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. Walker was limited during the first two practices of the week before completing Friday's session without a game-status designation on the team's published report. The subsequent downgrade means his availability remains uncertain, although the available reporting does not establish whether he experienced a setback or explain the reason for the change. The Raiders host the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. Las Vegas will need to clarify Walker's status before the game, while his questionable designation leaves open the possibility that he could still play. home.headline: Jack Bech’s status for Week 8 against New York Jets unclear on Las Vegas Raiders’ final injury report
home.blurb: Bech, who has been on injured reserve with a broken right forearm since the Week 3 game against the New Orleans Saints, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Kubiak was asked if the wide receiver will be activated before the team's trek to the Big Apple, but the coach said they have until Saturday to make that decision, according to The Athletic's Sam Warren . In other Raiders injury news, backup edge defender Patrick Johnson (stinger) has been ruled out. That could lead to practice squad edge Cian Slone getting his third call-up in as many weeks. However, Slone has been a healthy scratch during the last two Sundays, and this would be his last call-up before the team has to add him to the 53-man roster if they want to elevate the undrafted rookie a fourth time. Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson (back) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice but was upgraded to limited on Friday and listed as questionable for Sunday. As for the Jets, their defensive line is pretty beaten up. Defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat (knee) and edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) have been ruled out, while rookie edge/second overall pick David Bailey (groin) is doubtful. Bailey didn't practice at all during the week. Additionally, running back Breece Hall (quad) and offensive lineman/former Raider Dylan Parham (knee) are questionable. Hall was limited in practice all week, and Parham was limited for the first two sessions but was a full-go on Friday. Jack Bech’s status for Week 8 against New York Jets unclear on Las Vegas Raiders’ final injury report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL TRENDING College football live updates (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matt Holder Fri, October 30, 2026 at 8:32 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders opened Jack Bech's 21-day practice window ahead of the Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets . However, Bech's game status is still unclear after the Raiders released the final injury report for the week and head coach Klint Kubiak held his Friday press conference. The 2025 second-round pick had five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown in the three games he played to begin the season, while also serving as a notable run blocker on the perimeter. If Bech can't play, then recently activated wide receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr. could see a good amount of playing time in what is expected to be his season debut. Thornton has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since the beginning of training camp, and Warren also reported that Kubiak said Thornton's workload in New York is to be determined.

The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) carries the ball in the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . Most are picking the Steelers to emerge as the winners of this divisional battle , but don't be shocked if this one comes down to the wire. Both teams go into this matchup not being taken seriously. Perhaps if one of the two dominated this game and pulled away on the scoreboard, then some experts might believe in them. If not, then no matter who wins or loses, this game might fail to gain respect. Either way, the Steelers need to take care of business in their home venue, but this might be their biggest test of the campaign yet. Cleveland hasn't beaten anyone special to this point in the season, but the same can be said for Pittsburgh. It will be interesting to see how the outcome of this game affects whoever eventually wins the AFC North. You would have to assume the victor of this game will be the early favorite to win the division this season. It's not going to be an easy battle to win, and the high stakes only intensify this rivalry. Still Curtain contributors predict a Pittsburgh Steelers season defining victory "The Cleveland Browns have performed better than anyone expected this season but predicting them to sweep the Steelers this season feels rich. The Browns haven't won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003. Worse yet for Cleveland, they haven't swept the Steelers during the regular season since 1988. Mike McCarthy isn't going to let that happen on his watch." - Tommy Jaggi (Steelers 24-17) "Cleveland is surely talking a big game, and it would be awfully embarrassing to prove their words right. To be frank, neither of these teams is as good as their 5-2 record, but this still feels like it has the makings of a good game. If Pittsburgh loses, it will be a bitter pill to swallow. I think they put the Browns back in their place with a close win." - Andrew Falce (Steelers 24-20) "The Pittsburgh Steelers don't want to squander a chance to give Mike McCarthy his first taste of ranking first in AFC North with a win against the Cleveland Browns. Patrick Graham's defense plays a lot better than in Week 4, forcing DeShaun Watson to make slower, harder decisions as a QB. Aaron Rodgers and Jaylen Warren lead McCarthy's offense to an effective afternoon." - Loyal Ricks Jr. (Steelers 28-20) Final prediction has Steelers finding a way to squeak out a win Score Prediction: Steelers 23, Browns 20 Everyone should predict this AFC North clash to be a close game that comes down to the wire. Expect turnovers to be monumental in the outcome of this game. The Steelers offense needs to play a smart brand of football. Establish the run early and take care of the football. Any opportunities they give the Browns based on Pittsburgh shooting themselves in the foot could be costly. Cleveland has struggled against lesser foes this season but so have the Steelers. That being said, overall, the Black and Gold have the edge when it comes to the talent on their roster. Trusting Aaron Rodgers to win the game over Deshaun Watson provides a clear edge. This won't be an easy game to win, but if the offense can have a strong rushing attack and take care of the football, then they should have a steady path to victory. On the defensive side of things for Pittsburgh, it's all about creating havoc for the opposition. Stop the run first and get Watson on the ground often. Create dysfunction for the quarterback and don't allow him to escape the pocket for big gains. Forcing a couple of turnovers and winning the turnover margin will be vital to getting a win. It's easier said than done, but the Steelers have the players to make this happen. At the end of the day, pick the Steelers to win this AFC North matchup. It's not going to be pretty, as these two teams are eerily similar at this point in the season. Neither has done terrific things thus far, but they have found a way to get to impressive 5-2 records. The Steelers have the talent to win this game, and there should be a strong chance that they do as long as they take care of the ball. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. away.blurb: Most notably, Browns defensive end Jared Verse (knee), who did not practice on Wednesday, was able to take part in a limited practice on Thursday. That's good news, as he absolutely has to be on the field for Sunday's game in Pittsburgh. After the Week 4 victory on a Thursday night, Verse endeared himself to Browns fans everywhere by trashing some of the Steelers players, calling them "dirty". He automatically gained likability among all Cleveland fans, as a result. Browns offensive tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) suffered a concussion in the Week 7 game against the Tennessee Titans, and he has not practiced this week in either session. That's the bad news. The good news is that he was the only 'DNP' for Thursday's practice. Rolling down the line, safety Grant Delpit (neck), defensive tackle Mason Graham (ankle), defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring), center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle), safety Daniel Thomas (ankle) and Verse were each limited participants on Thursday. After a limited practice on Thursday, running back Dylan Sampson (knee) was able to take part in a full practice session, and it appears he is trending toward another meaningful role in his second game back from the reserve/injured list. Gabriel was activated from the reserve/injured list, and he has been practicing in full for several weeks, as the Browns have figured out a way to keep all four quarterbacks without exposing any to the practice squad and/or having to lose them for the season on IR. home.headline: Thursday injury report for the Browns in Week 8 against the Steelers
home.blurb: Thursday provided major relief as two key starters upgraded from Wednesday's DNP list. Starting center Elgton Jenkins and rookie edge rusher Jared Verse both returned to the field in a limited capacity after sitting out Wednesday. They join safety Grant Delpit, interior defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., linebacker Carson Schwesinger, and defensive backs Myles Harden and Daniel Thomas, who all maintained their limited status. Sophomore running back Dylan Sampson upgraded from limited on Wednesday to a full participant on Thursday, clearing any lingering concerns regarding his knee as he looks to provide firepower to the Cleveland backfield. Thursday injury report for the Browns in Week 8 against the Steelers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL TRENDING College football live updates Thursday injury report for the Browns in Week 8 against the Steelers Lane Dobbins, Browns Wire Fri, October 30, 2026 at 9:55 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Thursday's injury report brought positive developments for the Cleveland Browns as they prepare to travel to Acrisure Stadium for a Week 8 clash against the Pittsburgh Steelers. While no new players were added to the report, three key contributors earned upgrades, highlighted by edge rusher Jared Verse and center Elgton Jenkins returning to practice, and tailback Dylan Sampson taking another step forward. Here is Thursday's updated practice participation breakdown for Week 8. Right Tackle Tytus Howard (Concussion) Starting right tackle Tytus Howard was the lone absence on Thursday as he remains in concussion protocol. If he cannot clear the protocol by Sunday, we should expect Dawand Jones to start in his stead. Defensive Tackle Mason Graham (Ankle) Defensive Tackle Mike Hall Jr. (Ankle) Cornerback Myles Harden (Hamstring) Linebacker Carson Schwesinger (Ankle) Defensive Back Daniel Thomas (Ankle) Defensive End Jared Verse (Knee) Running Back Dylan Sampson (Knee) With 9 of the 10 listed players now practicing in some capacity, Friday's final report and game status designations will set the stage for Sunday's divisional battle in Pittsburgh. My Falcons vs. Buccaneers prediction focuses on Tampa's struggling passing attack, Atlanta's underlying matchup advantages, and weather that could influence several of my favorite betting angles. Check out more NFL picks for Week 8. TOP PICK Falcons vs Buccaneers prediction: Falcons +2.5 I'm fading the market and playing the Atlanta Falcons +2.5, playable down to their opening line of +1.5 . Typically, you want to fade the previous week's results, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers just waxed the Carolina Panthers 43-13 last week. Baker Mayfield returned Sunday from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb and wasn't asked to do much in Tampa's victory. He completed just seven of 11 passes for 64 yards. Mayfield has the third-worst QBR this season , so I don't trust him to win by a significant margin. Meanwhile, Atlanta has better yards-per-play, early-down EPA per play, quarterback pressure rate, and explosive-play rate differentials , despite the teams having played similarly difficult schedules and both starting quarterbacks having missed time due to injuries. Falcons vs Buccaneers combo Unlike Atlanta's spread, I'm following the line movement here by taking the Under 43.5 , with the total dropping from its 45.5-point opener to the current number. The projected pace, playing styles, and weather all support the Under cashing . For instance, the Falcons rank 25th in seconds per play on offense, while Tampa Bay ranks 30th. Per Nfeloapp.com , Atlanta has the third-lowest pass rate over expectation, while the Bucs have the fifth-lowest rate. The forecast calls for windy, rainy conditions in Tampa on Sunday, which could hinder both passing and kicking games and make these teams more likely to lean on their rushing attacks. I'll discuss my third combo leg (Baker Mayfield Under 224.5 passing yards) below. Baker Mayfield Under 224.5 passing yards Falcons vs Buccaneers touchdown scorer: Kyle Pitts Sr. I love Atlanta TE Kyle Pitts Sr.'s anytime touchdown price, and I'd trade it up to 27% . Pitts leads Atlanta with four touchdown catches this season , and he torched Tampa Bay in their final meeting last year, hauling in 11 catches for 166 yards and three scores. The matchup is still favorable. The Bucs have allowed the fifth-most touchdowns to opposing tight ends with five , while the middle of their defense has struggled in coverage. Bijan Robinson and Drake London also command plenty of attention, potentially leaving Pitts isolated against linebackers and safeties. I'll take Pitts' athleticism in those one-on-one matchups near the goal line. picks.blurb: Our Buccaneers vs. Falcons Score Predictions Are In - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Our Buccaneers vs. Falcons Score Predictions Are In Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles looks on before the game between the Cowboys and the Buccaneers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect River Wells, Caleb Skinner, Collin Haalboom, James Hill & Logan Robinson Sat, October 31, 2026 at 2:22 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a must-win game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn't been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don't believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield's thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs' offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs' record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles' rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta's passing attack, it looks nice. It's going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. River Wells, Editor: Falcons 24, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way - Tampa Bay will have to go through the air. I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own - Bucs drop this one in Raymond James. Consensus: Falcons 3, Bucs 2 This is among the closest prediction slates we've had all year. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year. The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Tampa Bay on Nov. 1. picks.blurb: NFL Expert Picks: Who will win in Week 8, Falcons or Buccaneers? Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE FREDDIE FALCON MERCEDES-BENZ STADIUM Training Camp The Falcons play the Buccaneers for the first time this season on Sunday. It's their last division matchup before closing the year with three straight NFC South games. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the 66th time on Sunday, reigniting a series that has been exceptionally close. Atlanta leads the head-to-head 33-32, and each of the last six games between the two teams has been decided by six points or fewer. That includes the Falcons' 29-28 victory last season in Week 15, which featured a 15-point, fourth-quarter rally by Atlanta and a career game from tight end Kyle Pitts. Both teams head into this game off rejuvenating wins. A potent rushing attack that generated 258 yards on the ground and a defense that created four turnovers propelled the Buccaneers to a 43-13 win against the Carolina Panthers. The Falcons also forced four turnovers and got a strong performance from quarterback Michael Penix Jr. to earn a 29-20 win and hand the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season. After the Panthers lost to the Green Bay Packers Thursday night, the Falcons would gain sole possession of first place in the NFC South with a victory on Sunday. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and Buccaneers. away.headline: Falcons rule out 2 players, elevate 2 from practice squad vs. Bucs
away.blurb: The Atlanta Falcons made some last minute tweaks to their roster ahead of Sunday's NFC South matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . First, the team ruled out cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. and linebacker Divine Deablo. Both players sat out last weekend against the San Francisco 49ers and were listed as questionable on Atlanta's final Week 8 injury report. With Deablo out, the Falcons will turn to rookie Kendal Daniels to wear the green dot on defense. Herbert will replace Brian Robinson Jr., who was ruled out due to a hamstring injury. Check out the team's updated 53-man roster and practice squad for NFL Week 8 below. This article originally appeared on Falcons Wire: Falcons rule out 2 players, elevate 2 from practice squad vs. Bucs Daniels had a breakout performance in Week 7, recording two turnovers including the game-clinching interception in the fourth quarter. Atlanta will also look to rookie linebacker Harold Perkins Jr. to start alongside Daniels on Sunday against the Buccaneers. The Falcons also announced two practice squad elevations for some extra reinforcements. According to the team, running back Khalil Herbert and linebacker Brian Asamoah will join the team's 53-man roster in Week 8. Both players were elevated last week, and it's no surprise to see them back with the injuries at linebacker and running back. away.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. It’ll come down to who executes better and the Buccaneers have a golden opportunity to make a statement in a game that could have massive implications for the NFC South race. 4 key matchups to watch as Buccaneers face the Falcons in Week 8 5 Buccaneers who need to thrive in Week 8 vs. Falcons Panthers’ loss to Packers just gave the Buccaneers a golden opportunity in NFC South Todd Bowles had the perfect message for the Buccaneers after blowout win over Panthers Buccaneers down several key players as latest injury report paints ugly picture This article was originally published on thepewterplank.com as Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of We

away.blurb: Avieon Terrell and Olamide Zaccheaus did return to practice in limited fashion. In the game, the Falcons got a lot out of the players who filled in. Khalil Herbert was elevated to the game day roster ahead of Sunday's matchup. Acting as Bijan Robinson's backup, Herbert got a couple carries that were impactful within drives that resulted in points. home.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. home.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
home.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). picks.blurb: Jaguars vs. Colts: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Jaguars vs. Colts: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 8 JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 7: Brenton Strange #85 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs the ball during the fourth quarter of an NFL 2025 game against the Indianapolis Colts at Everbank Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Gus Logue Sat, October 31, 2026 at 5:11 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome to Big Cat Country's staff roundtable! This week, we're previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars' second divisional matchup of the season. They look to extend their 11-game home win streak against the rebuilding Indianapolis Colts. Question 1: What's your top question/concern about the Jaguars this week? Dillon Appleman : Can they stop playing down to their competition? In their last two games, the Jaguars have lost to the Texans and were eight seconds away from losing to the Eagles. Those two opponents have a combined record of 4-10 this season, so it's fair to question if they have a problem with elevating their game when the competition is poor. The Colts fit that same mold as a team that has basically punted on the season already, so I would like to see a more focused Jaguars team as they look to take a stranglehold over the AFC South. Travis Holmes : The Jaguars have been one of the NFL's top run-stopping defenses over the last two seasons. But as my college coach always tells me, you're only as good as your last game played. Can Anthony Campanile's unit rebound from the 114-yard rushing performance it surrendered against the Houston Texans before the bye week? One major strength-versus-strength matchup to watch is that the Jaguars rank second in the NFL in explosive rushing gains allowed, surrendering just 7 over the first six games, while the Colts' offense ranks eighth with 23. Limiting Jonathan Taylor is the first test. Eliminating the game-changing runs is the second. Gus Logue : Can Jacksonville's secondary survive without Antonio Johnson? He should be back soon from his ankle injury, but with No. 3 safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve, depth is a concern at the position. The good news is that the limping Colts probably aren't equipped to do anything about it. But could another worrisome game from the secondary spark a trade for a veteran to help solidify the unit, the way that Jakobi Meyers did for the passing offense last season? Henry Zimmer : My top questions are simply about if the Jaguars are going to add any talent at the deadline. Trades within the AFC South are not happening, but can the Jags get better by adding a player late? Defensive line help comes to mind first, but does adding someone there benefit or hurt in the long run? Question 2: What's the key to a Jaguars victory this week? Dillon : The key to a Jaguars victory is to simply keep Jonathan Taylor from wrecking the game. The Colts are just 3-6 all-time against the Jaguars with Taylor in the backfield, but all three wins have come when Taylor has gone for over 100 yards. He drives the success of that offense, so the key is to prevent a big day, which should be expected considering the Jaguars' dominance against the run under Anthony Campanille. Travis : Establishing the run game seems to be the primary focus heading into this week's matchup. The Colts rank 22nd in the league in opponent rushing yards allowed per game, and that was before Indianapolis decided to trade away interior game-wrecker DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Considering the Indianapolis front seven's struggles with missed tackles and Bhayshul Tuten's propensity to force them, this seems like a match made in heaven, especially with a potentially rainy Sunday in Duval. Gus : Quarterback play in high-leverage situations. I think we could end up looking at the box score and saying, "See, 150 rushing yards for the Jaguars and 50 rushing yards for the Colts, that's where the game was won/lost!" But really — as much as I do expect the Jaguars to have success on the ground and the Colts to struggle on the ground — Jacksonville will win because they have the better quarterback to move the chains. Henry : The key to victory this week is playing simple. This is a Colts team that is nuking itself into oblivion and should be a pushover. Don't make this game complicated and win outright. No need for jet sweeps on the half-yard line to a backup tight end. Trevor Lawrence should be out of this game in the fourth quarter. Make it simple. Question 3: Who will be an X-factor for the Jaguars this week? Dillon : I have a giant microscope over the Colts' rookie left guard, Jalen Farmer, vs. the Jaguars' interior defensive line. After the Colts traded away perennial Pro Bowler Quenton Nelson, the Colts will be starting Farmer, who has all of three offensive snaps this season. I'm looking for a big day for Arik Armstead and/or Ruke Orhorhoro on Sunday. Travis : My X-factor for this week is Jacksonville rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon, who will face off against Colts interior defensive linemen Grover Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore . Pregnon has shown major promise throughout 2026, with only a few bumps along the rookie road. Adebawore, who the Colts seem to be doubling down on moving forward following the DeForest Buckner trade, has significantly improved his hand placement and quickness in 2026. If there's an area of concern for the Jacksonville offense, it's more than likely going to come from Indianapolis' interior defensive line. Gus : Chris Rodriguez Jr., who finished with 11 carries for 55 yards in Week 6 compared to 12 carries for 39 yards for Bhayshul Tuten. I certainly expect Tuten to operate as Jacksonville's lead back moving forward, and even to have a very productive second half of the season, but don't forget about Rodriguez. Liam Coen wants this backfield to be a 1-2 punch. I could see C-Rod having a solid 50-yard, 1-TD outing on Sunday. Henry : Against a downtrodden Colts team, can the Jags manufacture some catches for Brian Thomas Jr. to potentially bolster his trade status before the deadline? This would be a lovely conspiracy if the Jags targeted BTJ upwards of a dozen times to get him maybe over 100 yards on the day and then immediately look to trade him. Strike while the iron is hot! away.headline: Colts now open to dealing RB Jonathan Taylor for significant draft picks, per report
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are listening to trade offers for star running back Jonathan Taylor , who could be the best player available at the trade deadline and fetch a significant price. His big-play ability has been limited somewhat this season because of the loss of deep threat Alec Pierce, but Taylor has 587 rushing yards, and he's tied for the NFL lead with eight rushing touchdowns. ESPN has reported that the team was reluctant to trade the superstar back, then changed that report on Saturday with a report that the Colts are willing to trade Taylor. But the franchise's position on Taylor has not changed. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Indianapolis first sent a signal to the rest of the NFL that the franchise was headed for a rebuild when franchise owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon fired general manager Chris Ballard after the team's loss to the Titans, and the Colts acknowledged that position by trading two franchise pillars, left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, to the 49ers on Tuesday. Taylor is obviously the team's best asset, the kind of finishing piece who could push a contending team over the top. When he's healthy, Taylor has always been one of the league's best weapons. He's scored a franchise-record 77 rushing touchdowns, and his 8,185 rushing yards are second only to Edgerrin James (9,226) in Colts' history. Unlike slot receiver Josh Downs, who requested a trade earlier this week, Taylor has not requested a trade. “You can’t control some things,” Taylor said this week after initially trying to brush aside trade speculation. “The business side is going to move with or without you, with or without your permission, with or without you knowing.” The Colts are not actively shopping Taylor, either. Indianapolis doesn't have to shop anybody at this point. The Nelson and Buckner trades made it clear the Colts are willing to deal. Denver, Green Bay, Minnesota, Seattle and the New York Giants are among the teams interested in Taylor's services. But the Colts do not want to let Taylor go for nothing. Unlike Nelson and Buckner, who were in the final year of their contracts, Taylor is signed through 2028. Taylor's contract makes him an attractive trade piece because the Colts have paid his $15 million signing bonus, leaving a new team responsible for his remaining 2026 base salary, $15 million in 2027 and $9.46 million in 2028. Indianapolis has held firm on its requests so far. The Colts have turned down a second-round pick and an additional draft pick for Taylor, according to a report from The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . The obvious comparison for a Taylor trade is the deal the 49ers made for Christian McCaffrey at the deadline in 2022. San Francisco sent a second, third, fourth and fifth-round draft pick to Carolina to get McCaffrey, who had a longer injury history than Taylor. home.blurb: Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out The Jacksonville Jaguars secondary could be stretched Sunday, as the team has ruled out safety Antonio Johnson for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Friday after initially suffering his ankle injury in the second quarter of the team's Week 6 London matchup versus the Houston Texans. His absence clearly puts more pressure on a safety room that has already dealt with attrition earlier this season with Eric Murray, who dealt with a Week 4 concussion that kept him out of Week 5. Those combined injuries, between weeks 5 and 6 resulted in safety Kaevon Merriweather playing increased snaps on defense: With Johnson now out, the expectation is that Merriweather will receive his first start of the 2026 season. Liam Coen discussed Merriweather in Friday's media availability. In addition to the Johnson update, wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) also did not practice on Friday and is listed as questionable, though he spoke with Florida Times Union's Demetrius Harvey following practice, advising that he "felt okay." Meyers was listed on Wednesday and Thursday's injury report as a limited participant with only a hamstring issue, before sitting out Friday's session with an additional ankle issue that would have presumably occurred on Thursday. His status could come down to game day, with rain and a wet field in the forecast for Sunday. Running back LeQuint Allen Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Josh Hines-Allen (ankle), linebacker Jahlani Tavai (hamstring), and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were all limited on Friday and carry no game-day injury designation. Additionally, cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring), defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro (ankle), and tight end Brenton Strange (eye) were each full participants and expected to play. Notably, there has been no update on the 21-Day windows being opened for offensive lineman Patrick Mekari (back), rotational edge BJ Green (elbow), or rookie defensive end Zach Durfee (upper body). Each player has been on the injured reserve for at least four weeks, with the potential to return as the team comes off the Week 7 bye week. The Colts, on Friday, ruled out wide receiver and starting punt returner Anthony Gould (concussion). Gould is out even though he practiced fully on Thursday and Friday. Additionally, starting slot cornerback Justin Walley (knee) is out Sunday after not practicing all week. Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) are both questionable. Boettcher has not practiced all week. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. picks.blurb: Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Rams-Chargers preview: 5 questions for Sunday's matchup Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 1:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams are taking on the Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday in their first meeting since the 2022 season. The Rams are 3-4 and looking to get back to .500, while the Chargers are still searching for their first win. To preview this game, we caught up with Chargers Wire's Gavino Borquez and asked him five questions about the team, including a final score prediction. What on earth has happened to Justin Herbert and this offense? What's gone so wrong with Mike McDaniel as the OC? Chargers Wire: The Chargers sit at 0-6 and rank dead last in the NFL in points per game (15.0) and EPA per play (-0.190). Herbert is playing the worst football of his seven seasons in the league. He has thrown 5 touchdowns and thrown 8 interceptions, tying for the league high, and has taken 21 sacks. The issues are layered. The offensive line and wide receiver group have been ravaged by injuries. Pre-snap penalties have hindered the unit. And the marriage between Herbert and McDaniel's scheme has not clicked. The two spent roughly four hours in film sessions during the bye week working on mutual accountability and finding spots to build on. We will see if it comes together on Sunday. Are there any key players the Chargers are getting back from injury this week coming off the bye? Chargers Wire: Right tackle Joe Alt is officially cleared and returning to the lineup after missing time with a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has been a full participant in practice coming out of the bye, though still navigating final clearance from a concussion, and is expected to play. Who's an underrated player on defense that the Rams should know about? Chargers Wire: While the average casual fan might not know his name, defensive tackle Teair Tart is widely respected by offensive linemen as a player they need to account for. Tart is known for his run defense prowess, but he has flashed effectively in generating interior pressure. Do the Chargers have any playmakers who can threaten the Rams defense besides Ladd McConkey? Chargers Wire: The Chargers don't possess an alpha weapon, but second-year Tre' Harris has flashed potential as a reliable deep threat . In 5 games, he has caught 15 passes on 26 targets for 225 yards, averaging an efficient 15.0 yards per reception. Though his momentum was temporarily paused by an injury suffered in Week 5 that forced him to miss the Week 6 game against the Chiefs, Harris is trending towards on Sunday. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Chargers Wire: While the Chargers benefit from the return of key offensive pieces in Joe Alt and Ladd McConkey, their vulnerability lies right up the middle. The Bolts' struggling interior offensive line is poised to be the Achilles' heel in this game, allowing the Rams' defensive front to consistently collapse the pocket and get to Justin Herbert. Furthermore, even with the Chargers coming off a bye week, it's hard to tell whether they've made any meaningful offensive changes. Expect the Rams to exploit the center of the line and for their balanced offense to score three touchdowns to secure the victory. Rams 24, Chargers 16. away.headline: Chargers placing S Derwin James on IR
away.blurb: James, 30, is the former 17th overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft by the Chargers out of Florida State. He finished the fourth year of a four-year, $12.388 million rookie contract that included a $7.090 million signing bonus. The Chargers announced they are placing S Derwin James on injured reserve. Los Angeles also signed CB Isas Waxter to the active roster and moved CB Kaiir Elam from the practice squad. He returned in 2021 after missing all but five games of the 2019 season and missed the entire 2020 season due to injury. The Chargers then picked up his fifth-year option back in April of 2021. James later signed a four-year, $76.4 million extension with the Chargers back in 2022. He was entering the final year of that deal and slated to make a base salary of $14.5 million in 2026 when he signed a three-year, $75.6 million extension through 2029. In 2026, James has appeared in three games for the Chargers and recorded 21 total tackles and one pass deflection. Want more articles like this? away.headline: Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams
away.blurb: Safety Derwin James Jr. remains out with a hamstring injury. This week, he reportedly had a setback, and as a result, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he’s a candidate to go on injured reserve. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) also won’t play. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have hamstring injuries, are questionable for Sunday’s contest. Garrett will be out on Sunday, as will wide receiver Davante Adams. At times, the Rams have struggled defensively — they gave up 302 passing yards last week against the Las Vegas Raiders — so perhaps there is a slight opening for the Bolts to find some success. There isn’t a whole lot the Los Angeles Chargers can do right now, or even by the end of the season, to play a lot better. The most immediate thing that would help is for them to become healthier. Starting right tackle Joe Alt hasn’t played since Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks due to a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a concussion during L.A.’s last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6, and he entered concussion protocol as a result. Both men returned to practice for the Chargers this week, and there is good news about their status for this Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. Alt and McConkey are on the mend In the Chargers’ final injury report for Sunday’s game, neither Alt nor McConkey are listed, which means both are expected to play, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic. While the Chargers are 0-6 and have been a disaster, the Rams haven’t exactly lived up to expectations either. The Rams have a 3-4 record despite being strong favorites to win the Super Bowl championship when the season started, and while they have had some injuries, such as the one that reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is dealing with, they have their own problems. The Bolts currently rank last in the NFL in points per game, 28th in passing yards and last in turnovers. Quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions heading into Week 8 with eight, against just five touchdown passes. Star wide receiver Ladd McConkey didn't practice on Monday as he recovers from a concussion. Fellow wideout Brennen Thompson also is dealing with an injury, with his quadriceps as the issue. However, Tre Harris looks ready to come back from his hamstring injury. Which can become a huge boost for struggling quarterback Justin Herbert, who has thrown more interceptions at eight compared to touchdown passes with five. But the Chargers, again, face potential roster tinkering ahead of the league's trade deadline. Herbert has risen as a possible trending trade contender, especially with the Seattle Seahawks becoming linked as a possibility there . home.headline: Los Angeles Rams Receive Direct News Connected to Micah Parsons
home.blurb: According to a report from longtime NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Micah Parsons is targeting a return to the field for the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams. Matthew Stafford and the Rams' offensive line will be going up against one of the best pure pass rushers in recent NFL history. Assuming he does return, the offensive game plan will need to change drastically from what it would have been had Parsons not played. On the Los Angeles side of things, the Rams are certainly hoping that their own superstar pass rusher will be back on the field. Myles Garrett has missed all games since Week 1 due to a knee issue of his own. He has been expected to return to the practice field at some point in the near future. All of that being said, the game against Green Bay is still weeks away. The Rams will need to take care of business this week against the Chargers before taking on both the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals. After that, the return of Parsons will be on deck.
