As they continue trying to stay afloat amid mounting injury problems, every game is extremely important. While the focus is on the Chargers this week, another report broke that directly impacts a future game on the schedule. Parsons has missed a lot of time for the Packers since suffering a torn ACL and a fully torn meniscus last season against the Denver Broncos late in the year. Green Bay has focused on bringing him along slowly, while focusing on getting him back to fully 100 percent before returning to the field. Needless to say, the likelihood of going up against Parsons will change a lot for Los Angeles in that game against the Packers. In his first season with Green Bay last year following the shocking blockbuster trade between the Packers and Dallas Cowboys, Parsons showed why the team gave up two first-round picks and Kenny Clark. He racked up 41 tackles, 12.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, and a defended pass in 14 games played. It's always good to see NFL stars healthy and on the field. For Los Angeles, it would have been more ideal to be able to avoid Parsons, but that likely won't end up being the case.

home.headline: Rams Midweek Report: Biggest Trade Deadline Need Has Become Painfully Obvious
home.blurb: As the Los Angeles Rams near the trade deadline , it has become increasingly clear that the team needs a WR3. While they primarily operate out of 13 personnel, the Rams still use three wide receiver sets at a 55.9 percent rate. It’s true that they are set to get Davante Adams back in approximately six weeks. However, they still lack depth behind Puka Nacua should he miss more time due to injury. However, we can’t keep living in a world from two years ago. The Rams and head coach Sean McVay have let everyone know what they think of Atwell and it isn’t as a WR2 or WR3 in the offense. Despite paying Atwell $10 million that was fully guaranteed, Atwell had six receptions total last season. This year, he has three. It’s clear that the Rams see Atwell as nothing more than a vertical clear-out player. That has value in an offense, but it’s also replaceable. While Thomas would fit the need as the Rams’ “X” receiver when Adams is out, his fit becomes a lot more complicated after that. Meanwhile, Downs would fit in the offense alongside Adams and Nacua and may only cost a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Downs may have more of a market as teams look to add a wide receiver. We’ll see if the Rams get involved. For now, the interest appears to exist. RotoWire recently put together an impact index score to quantify how hard teams have been hit with injuries. The Rams ended up with a moderate score of 4.56, ranking ninth in the NFL in injury impact. However, the Rams have had $67.3 million in cap space out due to injury, which is the fifth-most. Davante Adams and Poona Ford have been the biggest contributors to that with Adams’ $28 million cap-hit and Ford’s $11.4 million. 1. Myles Garrett's Rams Return May Have to Wait Until After the Bye To be clear, this is only me speculating. While there had been reports that Garrett would return to practice this week, the Rams opted not to open his practice window . Given that the Rams are in Washington next week, it seems unlikely that Garrett will test his knee on that field. The Rams then play the Arizona Cardinals the following week. The Rams are likely to continue playing it safe. At this point, it’s hard to see Garrett coming back before the bye. If the Rams are without Shelton, it would likely be Beaux Limmer at center. Without Parkinson, the Rams would be limited in what they could do out of 13 personnel. It’s clear the Rams feel Max Klare isn’t ready. Cardona could miss Sunday’s game, especially as the team signed Jake McQuaide to the practice squad this week. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie was limited while Nate Landman and Desjuan Johnson were full participants. home.headline: Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams
home.blurb: Safety Derwin James Jr. remains out with a hamstring injury. This week, he reportedly had a setback, and as a result, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he’s a candidate to go on injured reserve. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) also won’t play. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have hamstring injuries, are questionable for Sunday’s contest. Garrett will be out on Sunday, as will wide receiver Davante Adams. At times, the Rams have struggled defensively — they gave up 302 passing yards last week against the Las Vegas Raiders — so perhaps there is a slight opening for the Bolts to find some success. There isn’t a whole lot the Los Angeles Chargers can do right now, or even by the end of the season, to play a lot better. The most immediate thing that would help is for them to become healthier. Starting right tackle Joe Alt hasn’t played since Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks due to a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a concussion during L.A.’s last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6, and he entered concussion protocol as a result. Both men returned to practice for the Chargers this week, and there is good news about their status for this Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. Alt and McConkey are on the mend In the Chargers’ final injury report for Sunday’s game, neither Alt nor McConkey are listed, which means both are expected to play, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic. While the Chargers are 0-6 and have been a disaster, the Rams haven’t exactly lived up to expectations either. The Rams have a 3-4 record despite being strong favorites to win the Super Bowl championship when the season started, and while they have had some injuries, such as the one that reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is dealing with, they have their own problems. The Bolts currently rank last in the NFL in points per game, 28th in passing yards and last in turnovers. Quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions heading into Week 8 with eight, against just five touchdown passes. home.blurb: Offensive guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) were once again non-participants. There was hope both could return this week, but they're slated to miss yet another week at this rate. Receivers Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) were full and limited, respectively. Having Harris back out there will be huge for the offense, but recent history tells us we can't be confident in McConkey's return lasting all that long. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is on pace to return from a hamstring injury and the Chargers will need him with fellow corner Deane Leonard still rehabbing a concussion. Veteran Donte Jackson returning to the field would also be huge for the cornerback room that continues to be wiped out by injuries. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak. The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule. How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time? picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Bet on the Chicago Bears to cover the spread on Monday night at sportsbooks On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes wild. It should be a good game, and if that holds true it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. The Chiefs placed Simmons on injured reserve after VP of Sports Medicine and Performance Rick Burkholder explained the injury . “Things happen,” Reid said . “That’s no reason he was put on IR. He’s got a bad back. He’s got to get that worked out. That’s the main thing.” “So the gist of the report was this: something I reported with Mike Garafolo on Sunday, as you mentioned, that Josh Simmons was asked to leave a team meeting by Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes,” Rapoport said . “It involved having his feet up on the desk. He said he needed to because of his back. He’s going through rehab, and they said, ‘Well, just get out of here and go rehab.’ He did not handle it well. He went and apologized after. “Then he was placed on injured reserve, and there are a lot of questions about Josh Simmons, who has as talented a left tackle as you could possibly get, he is a stud as a player. I don’t know if he plays for the Chiefs again. I don’t know when he plays for the Chiefs again. There’s nothing more important than protecting Patrick Mahomes. You have to believe in the person doing it, and until that happens, I don’t know that he’s out there.” That distinction matters. Teams will stand by a player through injuries and even through odd absences. However, that patience tends to run out once an organization believes the effort isn’t going both ways. That said, the old NFL adage has to matter at some point: Availability is the best ability. Simmons missed nine games in 2025, and he has already missed six more in 2026. That’s 15 missed games out of 23 possible. He’s played in just eight games since being selected with the last pick in Round 1 of the 2025 NFL Draft. He’ll miss at least three more games on injured reserve. So far, there’s been no indication Simmons will return to play in the 2026 NFL season. Perhaps Rapoport is trying to send a message to the young, talented Simmons on behalf of the Chiefs. A tense team meeting has added another layer, and now one of the NFL’s top insiders has weighed in with a troubling update. away.blurb: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL TRENDING College football live updates Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker is returning to the NFL at the age of 36. Tucker is considered to be one of the greatest kickers in NFL history, which makes sense considering he's made 89.1% of his field goal attempts. His time with the Ravens ultimately came to an end after he was accused of inappropriate behavior during massage sessions. The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists made accusations against Tucker, with two of the massage parlors claiming they banned him because of his behavior. "I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists." Tucker has conducted workouts with the Colts, Jets and Saints over the past two years. It wasn't until this Wednesday, however, that he landed a deal. According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star, the Chiefs are signing Tucker to their practice squad. BALTIMORE, MARYLAND – DECEMBER 12: Kicker Justin Tucker #9 of the Baltimore Ravens talks to his wife, Amanda Bass, before playing against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on December 12, 2019 in Baltimore, Maryland. Butker has made 11 of 16 field goal attempts this season. He had two crucial misses on Sunday night against the Seahawks. If Tucker outperforms Butker at practice, he could end up starting as early as this Sunday against the Broncos.

home.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
home.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. home.blurb: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Oct. 31 that the Chiefs downgraded cornerback Mansoor Delane to out with a shoulder injury and placed fellow cornerback L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve. Both had been listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Kansas City initially left the door open by designating him questionable. Sneed, meanwhile, was listed with a knee issue and practiced on a limited basis Thursday and Friday. His move to injured reserve creates a longer-term roster concern for Kansas City, but the immediate consequence is straightforward: neither cornerback will be available in Denver. home.blurb: Denver listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and defensive end Zach Allen (hip) — all starters — as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) following Wednesday's session. Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City. Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action. home.headline: Broncos place RB RJ Harvey on injured reserve
home.blurb: The Denver Broncos have placed second-year running back RJ Harvey (knee) on the short-term injured reserve and he will miss at least four games in the meantime, per NFL insider Ian Rapoport on Saturday. Harvey popped up on the injury list this week and was ruled out for Week 7 on Friday. Harvey has been a dynamic player for the Broncos , playing several different positions on offense. Harvey has played out of the wildcat, been an explosive rusher and a reliable pass-catcher through his first few years in the Broncos ' offense. At the soonest, Harvey will be eligible to return to the team for their Dec. 6 game against the Miami Dolphins. Through the first seven games of 2026, Harvey has rushed 25 times for 87 yards and one touchdown, and caught the second-most passes on the team (25) with the second-most receiving yards (217) behind wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. Harvey also has a receiving touchdown, per Pro Football Reference . The Denver rushing attack has struggled through the first seven games, as rookie running back Jonah Coleman just got off the injured reserve in Week 7, and veteran running back J.K. Dobbins has seen carries cut with Coleman and Harvey in the lineup together. In the meantime, the Broncos called up running back Cody Schrader from the practice squad to back up Coleman and Dobbins. With Harvey now on IR, Denver could be more aggressive in the pursuit of Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathon Taylor. The Broncos have been linked to Taylor after trade rumors emerged earlier this week, and the Colts are in a full-on fire sale after two big trades this week. The Broncos are set to play the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday at 2:25 pm. Social : Follow Broncos Wire on Facebook and Twitter/X ! picks.blurb: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. away.headline: AJ Brown injury update, latest news on Patriots WR's status for game vs. Dolphins
away.blurb: When asked Wednesday if he was still working on regaining his explosiveness after his return from IR, Brown said, "Sometimes I see it, and sometimes I'm pushing through." New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins after being unable to practice this week with a knee injury. The team confirmed the news Saturday after Brown missed practice on Thursday and Friday. Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for four games. He returned for the Patriots' last two contests but indicated he was playing through something in Week 7. Brown took more than 100 snaps in those games, which were played in a span of just five days. He was targeted 16 times and made six catches for 75 yards across the stretch. "I know, obviously, I'm working on something, but there's no excuses," Brown said. Patriots EVP of player personnel Eliot Wolf told Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein after acquiring Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in June the wide receiver had a " degenerative knee condition ." "It's a factor, but we examined him," Wolf told Epstein in June. "He's got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it." Wolf noted at the time Brown had missed just one regular-season game to a knee issue. Brown also downplayed the issue when asked about his knee health this summer. The Patriots are already missing Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins after the wide receivers were placed on injured reserve with shoulder and calf injuries, respectively. Pop Douglas was serving as the Patriots' WR1 in front of Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III with Brown absent from Thursday's practice, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . The Patriots also have wide receivers Chandler Brayboy, Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner and Ryan Miller on the practice squad . Brown' absence could put more pressure on the Patriots to improve their rushing attack. Quarterback Drake Maye has gained almost as much ground (211 yards) as top running back Rhamondre Stevenson (285 yards) through seven games.

It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

away.headline: Patriots add running back Lan Larison to 53, elevate former Dolphins wideout from practice squad
away.blurb: After downgrading running back TreVeyon Henderson and wide receiver A.J. Brown to out, the New England Patriots traveled to Hard Rock Stadium with insurance at both positions. Larison, 24, will serve as the third option in the running back room behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner after an illness thinned the depth chart. The 5-foot-11, 209-pound change of pace reverted to the practice squad in September after making his NFL debut versus the Seattle Seahawks. He caught two passes for nine yards and averaged 24.5 yards per kickoff return in the Super Bowl LX rematch, handling three snaps on offense and six snaps on special teams. Linebacker Christian Elliss and cornerback Carlton Davis III move forward with questionable game statuses for the Patriots following the downgrades, while offensive tackle Marcus Bryant will remain on injured reserve for the divisional matchup. The organization promoted running back Lan Larison to the 53-man roster and elevated wide receiver Ryan Miller from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins. Arriving in Foxborough as an undrafted free agent in 2025, Larison spent his rookie campaign on injured reserve following a foot injury. The UC Davis product cleared waivers at the 53-man deadline in August and was retained on the 17-man scout team at its formation. Two months later, he takes the open spot on the active roster. Miller, 26, signed to the Patriots’ practice squad midway through October after Romeo Doubs joined fellow veteran target Mack Hollins on injured reserve. The 6-foot-2, 217-pound standard call-up will head back to his former stomping grounds as the fourth healthy wide receiver behind DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. Currently ranking fifth on the Dolphins in receiving yards, Miller reeled in a season-long, 77-yard touchdown from quarterback Malik Willis before making his way to Gillette Stadium. Originally entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie in 2023, the Furman alum spent three years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before being claimed off waivers by the New York Giants and then by Miami during training camp. He has appeared in 30 NFL games, including six starts, while totaling 17 receptions for 254 yards and four touchdowns. Sunday’s kickoff in Miami Gardens is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

There are a bunch of different players to consider in this market, but the Eagles' offense has been banged up all year with DeVonta Smith (out) and Saquon Barkley (set to play despite a hamstring injury) missing time. That has thrust some lesser-known players into big roles, especially with Jalen Hurts out for the season with a blood clot. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee is set to make his third consecutive start, and the Eagles are looking to snap a five-game losing streak that has dropped them into third place in the division. Meanwhile, the Commanders are coming out of their bye week and looking to get back on track after a loss on Monday Night Football in Week 6 to the San Francisco 49ers. Jayden Daniels and company lost Terry McLaurin to a knee injury for the rest of the season in that matchup, which should lead to some new faces carrying the load for Washington at receiver. That opens the door for some interesting decisions in the anytime touchdown scorer market, and I've decided on three players that I like to score with these two rivals facing off. Overall, Barkley has suited up for just 32.8 percent of the Eagles’ offensive plays in the five games he’s appeared in, making him a risky bet elsewhere in the prop market. The star back played less than 16 percent of the snaps in Week 7, but he still handled nine touches for 71 yards and a score. The Commanders have only given up five rushing scores in six games, but they may struggle to contain Barkley, even if he’s at less than 100 percent. Stefon Diggs Anytime TD (+215) Stefon Diggs has four touchdown catches in five appearances in the 2026 season for the Commanders, and he’s now the No. 1 receiver with McLaurin done for the year. Diggs has played just 59.8 percent of the Commanders’ snaps on offense, yet he’s been targeted at least six times in every game. That’s led to 24 receptions for 214 yards, and Jayden Daniels has thrown the ball Diggs’ way a ton this season. In fact, Diggs found the end zone and had nine targets against this Philly team in Week 1. I’m buying him to have another big game on Sunday night, especially after he stepped up for six grabs and a score in Week 6. He has not found the end zone since, but the veteran tight end has remained a big part of the offense. That workload should eventually turn into some scores, and this is a great matchup for the Eagles tight end to make it happen. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions in the Commanders' Showdown With the Eagles, Starting With Jayden Daniels - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Nishant Gupta Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders get their rematch with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, and very little about it looks like the opener. Philadelphia won that one 24-22 when Washington's tying two-point try was stuffed. Since then, Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and the Eagles have lost five straight, their longest skid since 2016. Washington (1-4-1) comes off its bye after a 23-17 loss in San Francisco that also cost it Terry McLaurin, who tore his patellar tendon and is done for the season, according to the team . Head coach Dan Quinn called the week off "a much-needed reset in a lot of ways," per the team's website . Philadelphia (2-5) lost 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Commanders are about a six-point favorite at Northwest Stadium and hold the EPA edge in nine of 12 categories. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday Night Football. Jayden Daniels leads Washington in rushing Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) is hit as he throws by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Romello Height (94) during the second quarter at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Daniels has 213 rushing yards on 25 carries, 8.5 per attempt, in four games, and his 88.7 rushing grade ranks third among quarterbacks, according to PFF . He has played the last two games in a brace after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2, and he ran only four times for 10 yards in San Francisco. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Washington needs him to run. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury , leaving Rachaad White (36 carries, 145 yards) as the lead back. Philadelphia ranks 27th against the run at 131.4 yards per game, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards against the Eagles on Monday. Bold prediction: Daniels runs for 75 yards and a touchdown, more than any Washington running back. Washington sacks Tanner McKee four times Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh (98) sacks Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) during the first quarter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Quinn's defense blitzes more than any team except Minnesota, and it has only 11 sacks, tied for 22nd. "I'd love to see us, whether it's blitzing or rush coverage together, really being in sync with that," Quinn said Wednesday, per the team's website . Odafe Oweh leads the team with three sacks on 15 pressures, according to PFF , though he hasn't played up to his contract yet. K'Lavon Chaisson has 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. McKee is working behind a line that has allowed 18 sacks, and the Eagles had no sacks or quarterback hits of their own against Dallas. Bold prediction: Washington sacks McKee four times, even with Javon Kinlaw likely out with a knee injury. Antonio Williams beats Zack Baun this time Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams (14) makes a catch during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Week 1 belonged to Zack Baun. Washington targeted him six times in coverage, and its pass catchers finished with minus-2 yards against him, per Next Gen Stats. He added 12 tackles and was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week . Baun is still fifth among linebackers with a 79.5 grade, but he has allowed a 100.0 passer rating in coverage, according to PFF . With McLaurin out, the rookie is the receiver Washington needs to change the equation . Antonio Williams has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, and he caught four passes for 64 yards and a score in the opener. Bold prediction: Williams goes over 75 yards, and at least one of those catches comes with Baun in coverage. Sonny Styles forces a turnover Sept. 27, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles (52) gets the tackle and forces a fumble by Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (8) in the first quarter at Northwest Stadium. Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Sonny Styles leads Washington with 46 tackles and has an interception, a sack and a forced fumble. He made 13 tackles in San Francisco, per NBC Washington , and his 72.7 coverage grade ranks 10th among linebackers, according to PFF . Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th in EPA, and Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks all missed practice Thursday, per the Eagles . That could leave McKee leaning on Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon over the middle, where Styles does his work. Washington is plus-6 in turnover differential, second in the NFL . Bold prediction: Styles forces a fumble or picks off McKee. picks.headline: Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season
picks.blurb: Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 Mexico GP 2026 – Qualifying TRENDING College football live updates Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NFL Week 8 injury tracker Colts open to trading JT Belichick-Hudson breakup Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season NBC Sports Philadelphia Staff Sat, October 31, 2026 at 7:00 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Eagles at Commanders predictions for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Eagles (2-5) are on the road to face the Commanders (1-4-1) on Sunday Night Football. Let's get to our predictions: Reuben Frank (5-2) The Commanders aren't very good. They've won one game this year, they're 19th in the league in offense and 25th in defense. Their best running back is averaging 3.8 yards per carry, their best wide receiver is out for the year, their quarterback hasn't thrown a touchdown pass longer than 10 yards. They've already lost to two 2-5 teams, the Colts and Eagles, and they haven't beaten anybody in a month. I'm not sure there's a team I'd pick the Eagles to beat right now. Maybe the Dolphins. It's not really about who they're playing, it's about them. They aren't good at anything. They're the only NFL team ranked 27th or worse on both offense and defense. They don't make big plays on offense, they allow too many big plays on defense, they don't tackle, they don't pressure, they don't stop the run, they don't protect the quarterback, they don't run the ball consistently and they're bad on third down. They're just a bad football team. Do the Eagles have more talent than the Commanders? Sure. I don't think it's close. It doesn't matter. Commanders 24, Eagles 17 Dave Zangaro (6-1) The Eagles are heading to Washington this week to play a one-win Commanders team and are now 5 1/2-point underdogs! That's how bad this season has gotten. The Eagles finally showed some signs of life on offense last week and then the defense totally fell apart. Good teams find ways to win and bad teams find ways to lose; the Eagles are a bad team. Could they go to Washington this weekend and pull out a win? Sure. The Commanders stink too and are without some key players like Terry McLaurin and Jacory Croskey-Merritt. But the Eagles are even more banged up and it can be tough to stop a losing streak like this one. It wouldn't shock me if the Eagles win this game but I'm not picking it. Not after what I have seen the last few weeks. But maybe they can cover. Commanders 26, Eagles 24 Barrett Brooks (4-3) First things first, there is no way the defense plays as badly as they played last week against the Cowboys. Saquon Barkley set the tone early, allowing the offense to run the ball, which set up play action. Tanner McKee settled down in the offense using the quick game. You could see that Makai Lemon was comfortable being the first passing option. The defense felt embarrassed by the poor performance we witnessed on Monday. The trenches were poor all around against the run and the pass. There was too much freelancing in jumping gaps and no gap discipline. Linebackers played slow in their reads and no one was ready to tackle. The Cowboys' offense totally dominated us up front. They ran the ball right through the interior of the D-line. Monday's performance was an anomaly and not the norm of what we can expect from this Vic Fangio defense. Eagles 27, Commanders 21 Mike Mulhern (5-2) We've seen teams spiral downward under Nick Sirianni and he's sometimes powerless to stop it. After five straight losses and countless ways the season has been a disaster, Sunday night is setting up to be the final nail in the coffin of the Eagles 2026 season in front of another national audience. The Commanders are heavily favored, desperate to save their season, and coming off their bye. There is almost no reason to think the Eagles will rebound. But for some strange reason I have a feeling they will. The Eagles defense surely had their desire questioned after getting abused by the Cowboys. I expect them to bow up against a depleted Commanders offense. Washington is down Laremy Tunsil and Terry McLaurin for the season, plus top running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on IR. Jayden Daniels has been sacked 9 times in the last two games and a (finally?) healthy and motivated front should be able to get after him. The Eagles offense looked a step beyond competent against Dallas, though that likely had a lot to do with the opponent. Seeing Saquon Barkley back on the practice field on Friday was a big boost. He's going to try to power through his injuries again and this time he'll carry the Eagles to a win. Eagles 24, Commanders 23 Ashlyn Sullivan (5-2) For two weeks in a row, the Eagles' defense is the reason they lost the game. This matchup against the Commanders would typically be bad on bad – the Eagles offense vs Commanders defense. The Eagles' offense showed promising signs last week, the only silver lining for this team. Saquon Barkley has no injury designation and I was encouraged with the way the Eagles tried to run the ball against the Cowboys. The biggest matchup against the Commanders is the Eagles defensive line vs Commanders run game. The Commanders have not been able to run the ball effectively outside of Jayden Daniels' scrambles. I expect the Eagles defensive line to bounce back from their disappointing performance last week. More than anything, I am picking the Eagles to win this game because they can't lose six games in a row… right? Eagles 21, Commanders 17 Ryan Fowler (6-1) A lot of the country won't tune in to what many expect to be a snoozer on Sunday night, but make no mistake about it that this is a massive football game for both sides in primetime. For the Eagles, it would be great to see a full workload for Saquon Barkley. He was electric on Monday night against Dallas in the first half, and I think he gets back to his ways this week against a Washington front that could be missing a few starters (Javon Kinlaw has already been ruled out.) Away from Barkley, there has to be a plan this week to counter Washington's blitz-heavy defense. They send pressure at the second highest clip in football under DC Daronte Jones, and if the Eagles don't have a plan to get the ball out of Tanner McKee's hands, it'll be a long night. This is a defense that gives up a ton of yards and points, but they also take the ball away consistently to give their offense more possessions. Limiting turnovers will be huge. Defensively, last week was an outlier. It has to be an outlier. It was a historically bad night, and I think Vic Fangio's group comes ready to play in primetime. Overall, not that this isn't an important game for the Eagles — it obviously is — but this is a potentially organizational altering game for Washington. Coming off of a bye, at home, in primetime, being frank, I think Washington HC Dan Quinn loses his job if they don't win, and I think they are going to try and pull out all the stops to win in Week 8. Commanders 21, Eagles 17

away.headline: Saquon Barkley Injury Update: Eagles RB’s Week 8 Status Revealed
away.blurb: Saquon Barkley entered Week 7 with a hamstring injury that limited his workload against the Dallas Cowboys, and the running back suffered a back injury on Monday Night Football. Originally entering the league as the second-overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft , the Penn State product hit the ground running, recording 1,307 yards and 11 touchdowns as a rookie for the New York Giants. He remained an elite running back during his five years with the club before joining the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, where he immediately led the league with 2,005 rushing yards while playing a key role in the team's championship run. After missing a few weeks of action, Saquon Barkley returned to the field in a limited role and finished Week 7's loss with seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown to go along with two receptions for nine yards. While he only played nine snaps in the game thanks to the hamstring and back injuries, he will return to the field in Week 8. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Saquon Barkley is "good to go." Needless to say, this is great news for the Phialdelphia Eagles, as the entire offense is battling an absurd amount of injuries. Philadelphia's second- to fourth-string running backs are all injured, quarterback Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely, and wide receiver Devonta Smith will not play. Quite frankly, the Eagles have no choice but to run their offense through Barkley. While the team entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations, the absurd amount of injuries has them entering Week 8 with a 2-5 record. Saquon Barkley is a great player, but he probably can't carry a team this banged-up to the postseason, especially with the starting quarterback sidelined for the rest of the season.

away.headline: Eagles missing Saquon Barkley, 2 starting WRs at Thursday's practice
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Inquirer's Zach Berman noted the limited depth, suggesting that another roster addition might have been expected if Barkley were in serious danger of missing Sunday's game. However, not making another move does not guarantee Barkley will be available against Washington. None of the three has been ruled out for Sunday, but their continued absence from practice makes Friday's final injury report especially important. The Philadelphia Eagles could be without several important offensive contributors for Sunday's matchup against the Washington Commanders , with running back Saquon Barkley and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks absent from the portion of Thursday's practice open to reporters. ESPN's Tim McManus and Olivia Reiner said all three players were missing as Philadelphia began its first full practice of the week after Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The absences are particularly concerning because the team listed all three players as nonparticipants on Wednesday's estimated injury report. Philadelphia held a walkthrough Wednesday, so the participation designations were projections rather than based on actual practice activity. Philadelphia Eagles Barkley continues to deal with hamstring and back injuries after leaving Monday's loss to Dallas. The veteran returned against the Cowboys after missing two games with a hamstring issue, but his back tightened during the contest, eventually forcing him to the sideline. His absence Thursday adds to uncertainty in an Eagles backfield already depleted by injuries. Philadelphia placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve Wednesday, leaving Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue as the only other running backs on the active roster. Pierce emerged as a key contributor during Barkley's previous absence, leading the team's running backs with 151 offensive snaps over seven games. The Eagles promoted Blue from the practice squad Wednesday, but they haven't added another running back to the active roster. Philadelphia also continues to monitor Smith and Wicks, who missed Monday night's loss because of hamstring and ankle injuries, respectively. Their absences have put additional responsibility on rookie Makai Lemon, who caught his first career touchdown against Dallas, and the remaining members of the receiving corps. away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. The (5-2) Bears knocked off the New England Patriots 30 to 24 on Thursday Night Football, while the (4-3) Seahawks just won 20 to 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday night. Seattle's defense did a number on quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs offense, holding them out of the red zone for the first time in Mahomes' career. They also stymied K.C. running back Kenneth Walker III, who was the league's leading rusher heading into the week. On offense, the Seahawks ran the ball 41 times for 153 yards, but wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who has looked unguardable again this season, popped off for 9 receptions, 150 yards, and a touchdown. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook just put the odds up for the Monday night game in Seattle, and they have Chicago as the underdog at +3, with the money line at +144, and the over/under 46.5. Earlier today, it was Bears +3 and the money line at +136, so for perspective on how the oddsmakers view the Bears, before the Sunday night Chiefs at Seattle game kicked off, the previously unbeaten Chiefs were at +3 and +136 on the money line. The Bears just beat the defending AFC champion Patriots wire to wire in Soldier Field, but a trip northwest to face the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks will be the Bears' toughest test yet. away.headline: Bears Reveal Injury Designations for Two Key Offensive Targets
away.blurb: Tight end Colston Loveland was listed with a neck injury on Thursday's estimated injury report, which coach Ben Johnson said he hoped was a "minor thing." He was limited on Friday, then he was listed as a full participant on Saturday. On the Saturday injury report , Loveland had no injury designation for Monday—the best news the Bears could've gotten. The Bears did have bad news on their injury report, though, as running back Kyle Monangai will miss his fourth straight game as he deals with a turf toe and thumb injury. He didn't practice all week, so it wasn't a surprise that Monangai was ruled out again. Monangai's return is highly-anticipated for the Bears as he's popped up as a star running back this season. Maybe he'll be available in Week 9 versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, or the Bears will rest him until after the Week 10 bye. The Chicago Bears will face the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on "Monday Night Football." It would be a huge win for the 5-2 Bears to beat the Seahawks, who are coming off a big win over the Kansas City Chiefs. Chicago was worried about a couple of their offensive targets heading into Monday night's contest, though. Through seven games, Loveland ranks third in receiving yards (244 yards) on 26 receptions. He's scored two touchdowns. Monangai's injuries have caused a bigger problem than the team originally expected, though. Johnson said back on Oct. 16 that the team didn't see the need to place him on the injured reserve list, which would have required Monangai to miss at least four games. "It wasn't one of those things we felt like we needed to put him on IR for," Johnson said, via ESPN . "So, it's still week to week and as far as I know, he's trending in the right direction." Even though Monangai's only played in four games this season, he's posted the second-most rushing yards on the team (324) on 60 carries. He's scored three touchdowns.

Recovery runs on a sliding scale. A Grade 1 stretch heals in days to two weeks , a Grade 2 partial tear takes two to eight weeks, and a Grade 3 complete tear can sideline a player for six to 12 weeks or more, sometimes requiring surgery. That timeline is typical for an injury that required a specialist and a boot, while milder sprains resolve faster and higher-graded ones linger longer.
